problem: Leadership wanted the company to become self-organising.
title: Zappos adopts Holacracy and offers severance to those who are not on board
context: Zappos moved to a self-management system called Holacracy with no traditional managers.
decision_made: Adopt Holacracy company-wide and offer severance to staff who did not want to take part.
action_taken: CEO Tony Hsieh's March 2015 memo set an end-of-April deadline for the offer.
observed_outcome: About 14 percent of roughly 1,500 employees took the offer, and a later round brought the total departures to about 18 percent. Zappos said many took it for the money rather than because of Holacracy.
lessons: Major organisational changes can cause a large wave of departures, even when exits are voluntary.
limitations: Zappos's counter-view comes from an unverified internal document. The causes of departures are disputed.

claims.claim_text: Zappos offered severance to employees who were not on board with Holacracy.
Reports put departures at about 14 percent and later around 18 percent of the workforce.
